## Description
Modify the main fetch_content method to automatically detect feed type and route to appropriate handler (RSS parser or Jina AI).

## Tasks
- [ ] Rename existing `fetch_content` to `_fetch_html_content`
- [ ] Create new `fetch_content` that routes based on URL type
- [ ] Add feed type detection at fetch time
- [ ] Implement fallback to Jina AI for non-feed URLs
- [ ] Add logging for feed type detection
- [ ] Update sync_progress messages to indicate source type

## Acceptance Criteria
- RSS/Atom feeds use `fetch_rss_content()`
- HTML pages use `_fetch_html_content()` (Jina AI)
- Detection happens automatically without config changes
- Fallback to Jina works when feed detection fails
- Logs indicate which handler was used for each source
- All existing HTML sources continue working

## Implementation Flow
```python
async def fetch_content(self, url: str) -> Optional[Dict]:
    # Check if it's a feed
    if await is_feed(url):
        return await self.fetch_rss_content(url)
    
    # Fall back to Jina AI for HTML pages  
    return await self._fetch_html_content(url)
```

File to modify: `src/aisignal/core/services/content_service.py`

## Description
Create utility functions to detect if a URL points to an RSS/Atom feed and to identify the feed type.

## Tasks
- [ ] Create new file `src/aisignal/core/utils/feed_detector.py`
- [ ] Implement `is_feed(url: str) -> bool` function

- `is_feed()` returns False for HTML pages
- `get_feed_type()` distinguishes between RSS and Atom
- Functions handle malformed feeds gracefully
- Code passes linting (black, isort, flake8)

## Implementation Notes
- Use `feedparser.parse(url)` and check `feed.bozo` attribute
- bozo=0 indicates well-formed feed
- Use `feed.version` to determine feed type

```python
if await is_feed("https://blog.example.com/feed.xml"):
    feed_type = await get_feed_type("https://blog.example.com/feed.xml")
    print(f"Found {feed_type} feed")
```

This is a feature I want to implement in **release 0.10**

Whenever invoked in the UI, by pressing a command (l), the program wil look into the database, considering:
- notes for fully retrieved (interesting) resources
- resources marked as *removed*, with respect to the ratings that were proposed
- statistics of relevant resources and categories and sources they come from

An algorithm must be devised, to understand which categories or sources are _underperforming_. This could be a heuristic algorithm, starting from the statistics.

An AI based algorithm could review the content of the most relevant resources, or the ones that were dubbed as relevant manually, even if ranked low by the algorithm, and suggest new categories. Maybe new sources, as well?

A modal window should warn if incurring costs, probably making an estimate based on the amount of text that will be analyzed, and sent to the LLM.

The system should keep track of all operations on single reosurces:
- early removal (while in resource list view)
- removal while reading the short summary
- fetch of the full content
- generation of a summary or takeaway points
- adding a note
- removal after having fetched the content
- removal after having generated a summary/takeaway points
- removal after having written a note
- exporting it to obsidian
- sharing it

This should be transformed into an _interest_ quantity.

I should then keep all activities related to a resource in the database, and then device an algorithm, that 
will check:
- the alignment of each category 
- the alignemnt of sources
- possible new categories
- possible new sources
- modifications to the user's profile

The list of possible new sources should be generated beforehand, as a mixture of curated research from gihub awesome's lists, known blogs, or sources, known and respected authors' blogs, ... and an AI analysis of the user's profile.
From the list of possible sources, come the list of possible categories.

Selected sources and categories are a subset of the possible ones.

The users can move their interests in time. That's the idea.

body:
This is a feature I want to implement in **release 0.7**

Given the current algorithm of fetch and analysis:

> for each URL, there's a list of resources,
> - the content of the URL is transformed into markdown text, keeping the links
> - a diff_content is computed as diff of the live markdown content with the one stored in a db
> - the diff_content is sent to an AI with a detailed prompt, and all reources are extracted, with the title, link, the text that comes in the resource snippet, the categories the LLM finds more right, and a quantitative index made of three numbers (categories fit, profile fit, spam likeliness); the URL's diff_content is returned in a markdown format easily parseable;
> - the program parses the diff_content, extract a data structure for each resource, compute a unique quantitative index, from the three returned by the LLM, using a weighted average;

A possible point of optimization is to gather all diff_content from different URLs and send a single text to perform all analysis at once. diff_content should be grouped by URLs, using markdown header for the purpose. This will spare sending the context for each URLs.

In case tens or hundreds of URLs are monitored, this can be a bit extreme, especially when contents are not fetched for long periods (vacations, or when the laptop is not accessed), as the overall sum of diff_content can be too long.

There must be a mechanism to split the content into as few parts as possible, in order for the LLM not to have issues. Also, diff_content of a single URL should not be splitted, ever.
title: LLM requests optimization

body:
This is a feature I want to implement in **release 0.6**

The algorithm for selection is now this:
for each URL, there's a list of resources,
- the content of the URL is transformed into markdown text, keeping the links
- a diff_content is computed as diff of the live markdown content with the one stored in a db
- the diff_content is sent to an AI with a detailed prompt, and all reources are extracted, with the title, link, the text that comes in the resource snippet, the categories the LLM finds more right, and a quantitative index made of three numbers (categories fit, profile fit, spam likeliness); the URL's diff_content is returned in a markdown format easily parseable;
- the program parses the diff_content, extract a data structure for each resource, compute a unique quantitative index, from the three returned by the LLM, using a weighted average;

As of now all resources are added to the resources pool and to the DataTable in the MainScreen.

I want now to introduce two thresholds: a min and a max thresolds.

Only resources above the minimal threshold are added to the pool of resources, and then visualized in the DataTable in the MainScreen. All other resources don't even make it to the database, and are discarded.

More importantly, resources above the maximum threshold should be fetched, transformed into markdown directly and the markdown conten should go in the `full_content` field of the Resource class (and corresponding table in the DB).

These resources 
- should have a _greenish_ background for the whole row, when visualized in the datatable, with the green component growing as the quality approaches 100. A resource with 100 quality should have a 100% (255) value for the green component of the background. The red and blue components are up to you.
- A click on one of this resource (pressing enter, if using the keyboard), would show a Markdown Viewer widget where the content can be read. The Markdown Viewer would have the table of content on the right.
- the bindings when viewing the resource's content will be: (s)hare, (o)bsidian, (r)emove, (n)ote
- a note is a remark you can put into a area text in a modal, to express why you're interested in this resource, it will then be used to suggest profile or categories modifications;
- a remove will not remove the item from the db, but mark it as removed; the resource will never be visible, but its presence in the DB will be useful to provide feedback to your preferences and categories in the future.

For resources in between the two threshold:
- the background color should be _blueish_, with the same method to highlight more relevant resources (resources with a quality equal o the maximum threshold should be 100% blue)
- a click (enter) on a resource would only show the title, summary, category, like it is currently
- in this case, the bindings should be: (f)etch, (r)emove
- fetch would fetch the full markdown content of the resource and bring you to the previous case (the Markdown Viewer, with its bindings)
- a remove will not remove the item from the db, but mark it as removed; the resource will never be visible, but its presence in the DB will be useful to provide feedback to your preferences and categories in the future.
title: Double threshold mechanism

body:
Pressing Enter on a category will filter the items in the datatable.
Multiple categories can be selected. The behavior of the filter in this case is a boolean OR.
Items that are categorized with at least one of the selected categories are shown.

The same behavior is for Sources. The logic of multiple sources is OR.

The logic between Sources and Categories is a boolean AND. When both Categories are selected in the filters and Sources, then only items verifying the two conditions simultaneously are shown in the DataTable.

A _reset filter_ button, or switch should be available, whenever a filter is selected.
title: Filters in sidebar
